results.breaks: Removes the declared effect-size threshold, so any statistically significant difference however small would be called a demonstrated consequence. The threshold exists precisely to stop that, and it was declared before the locked run.
Lets any number of exclusions pass without the test being reported as underpowered, so a verdict could be drawn from two surviving pairs.
Picks the best-performing grid point as the confirmatory one instead of the preregistered point. That is the cherry-pick the preregistration exists to prevent.
results.old:
primary = next(t for t in tests
                   if t["family"] == "structural"
                   and t["magnitude"] == confirm["structural"])

results.breaks: Sorts the declared grid. Phase 3.1 measured crossing time to be non-monotone in fault rate, so ordering the grid is not a cosmetic change.
results.old: for magnitude in GRIDS[family]:       # declaration order, no sort

results.breaks: Turns the exact McNemar test one-sided, halving every p-value.
Fabricates a finite odds ratio when c = 0 by substituting 1 for the zero denominator. The real quantity is not finite and the preregistration says no point estimate is reported in that case.
results.old: "odds_ratio": None if c == 0 else round(b / c, 6),

results.breaks: Drops the flag that says the risk-difference interval is conditional on the discordant-pair count, so a reader would take it for a marginal interval.
results.new:

        "odds_ratio": None if c == 0 else round(b / c, 6),

"ci95_is_conditional_on_discordant_pairs": True,

results.breaks: Pins every lower confidence bound at zero.

results.breaks: Decides the conflict on response LABELS rather than classes, and stops counting 'nothing issued where a response was required' as a conflict -- which is the entire Phase-3.2 finding.
results.new: conflict = (correct_response not in kinds) if kinds else False
results.old: conflict = (want not in classes) if kinds else (correct_response != R_NONE)

results.breaks: Stops the matched nominal control from ever vetoing the verdict, so an H2 result could stand on a policy that escalates on clean flights.
Stops gating the evidence in the gated condition, so EG becomes EA and the study compares a condition against itself.
Stops detecting one class of invalid run, so scenarios the trust layer rejected samples in would be counted as valid data.
